equivalents.note: For maṇa the Tibetan uses yid, its usual word for manas, where it has sems for cia in 3b and throughout the commentary.

The Tibetan reads apā as the first person, bdag gis 'by me', the subject of mi shes 'do not know', not as the self that went and entered; its comment (cp.31.m2) cites the same bdag gis where Munidatta cites apā.

The Tibetan dmigs pa med, 'objectless', agrees with Munidatta's nirālamba (dmigs pa med pa in cp.31.m3) rather than nirāśa 'without hope'; likely only because dmigs pa med pa is also the glossary's Tibetan for anupalambha.
The Tibetan has bla ma'i drin las, 'by the guru's kindness', its phrase for guruprasāda (bla ma dam pa'i drin las in cp.31.m6), as if it read -prasādāt for gurusampradāyāt.

The Tibetan folds Munidatta's two clauses (goes to no-mind, enters clear light) into one, sems med pa 'od gsal la thim par 'gyur, 'dissolves into no-mind, clear light'; likely because sems med pa also means 'mindless, inanimate' and forms wherever sems is followed by med pa.

dngos po renders bhāva alone (dngos po cha shas med pa for bhāvasya niraṃśatā, and again for bhāvaṃ at the end of the segment), so this may belong under bhava-being, whose Tibetan is dngos po, rather than the pair.

questions: niralamba: the commentary (cp.31.m3) also renders nirālambena as dmigs pa med pa, directly before chos thams cad mi dmigs pa for sarvadharmānupalambha; I gave only the verse line. The glossary lists dmigs pa med pa under both niralamba and anupalambha, so the reviewer may want to settle which entry owns it.

cp.31.4a: the Tibetan has srid pa'i skyug bro, 'the disgust of existence', where the Bengali has bhaya ghiṇa, 'fear and disgust', as if it read bhava for bhaya; a search for bhava's srid pa would count this line although the Bengali has no bhava.

cp.31.5a: the Tibetan has rnam par dpyod par byed, 'examines', for bihariu ('roamed, sported'), so a search for vicara's rnam par dpyod pa will count this line although the Bengali has no vicāra here.
